content: We're doing a demo site for BonBon, as part of the docs, and as I was planning it out I remembered we did one for a "newly hired senior evangelist" at a ficitious Silicon Valley startup. This is what I love about AI tools. I couldn't remember her name or the name of the company but i remembered it was funny. So I explained the problem to Claude, and it gave me what I want. The new hire is Kim Parker, and she was hired by Bloatware. This is where having kept good records on the web comes in handy. A search engine wouldn't be much help because I didn't remember her name or the name of the company. And I wrote too much about Fargo for that to be a good search term. Instead my prompt was: "i wrote an app called fargo a few years ago and it had a demo site that was from a new hire at the company called Bloatware. can you find it for me on the web?" Got me what I wanted, and cited all the relevant links. It seems that Claude cares about the archives on the web more than the browser vendors do. There are important records there, not just notes about my latest creation in 2013.
